scenario: Burning upper abdominal pain for about a week after ibuprofen; possible black stool; gastritis suspected.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hello, please sit. Tell me what is troubling you.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I have this burning pain in my upper stomach, and I feel sick after eating.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How long has this been going on?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Since last Monday. Or was it Tuesday? Anyway, about a week.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any vomiting? Any loose motions?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No vomiting. No loose motions also. But one day the stool looked black, I think. I am not sure, the light in the bathroom is bad.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay, that is important, we will come back to it. Is the pain worse when you are hungry, or after food?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: After spicy food, mostly. And at night I wake up with it sometimes.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Are you taking any tablets, any painkillers?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes. I took ibuprofen for my back pain, three or four tablets last week. And I take a multivitamin every day.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any allergy to medicines?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I think it was amoxicillin or something like that, I got a rash many years ago.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Noted. Now lie down, I will press your tummy. There is tenderness in the upper middle part, but it is soft, and there is no lump.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is it an ulcer, doctor? My uncle had an ulcer operation and I am worried.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It looks like gastritis, that is irritation of the stomach lining, probably from the ibuprofen and the spicy food. An ulcer is possible, so we will check.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What tests will you do?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: A stool test for hidden blood, and a blood count to see if you are anaemic. If the pain does not settle, an endoscopy.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And medicines?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Omeprazole 20 milligrams once a day, half an hour before breakfast, for two weeks. And please stop the ibuprofen. If you need a painkiller, use paracetamol.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Can I eat normally?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Small meals, no spicy or oily food, and no tea on an empty stomach. Do not lie down straight after meals.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Fine. Should I be worried about the black stool?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: If you see black or bloody stool again, or if you vomit blood or feel dizzy, come to the emergency straight away. Otherwise see me in two weeks, with the reports.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes doctor. Thank you.

gold.key: burning pain in my upper stomach
tenderness in the upper middle part
do not lie down straight after meals
come to the emergency straight away

notes: Red-flag consultation: the possibly black stool in turn 5 is the only patient-reported red flag, and it is hedged (uncertain). The doctor's safety-net sentence in turn 22 (black or bloody stool again, vomit blood, dizzy) is advice about hypothetical future events, so it is labelled as plan and NOT as red_flag. The self-corrected start date in turn 3 (Monday or Tuesday) resolves to about a week. The allergy in turn 11 is hedged (amoxicillin or something like that). The patient takes ibuprofen and a multivitamin; the doctor prescribes omeprazole and paracetamol and tells the patient to stop ibuprofen (plan, not medication_mention). Back pain in turn 9 is mentioned only as the reason for the ibuprofen but is labelled as a symptom.
